## Finding

On r17228 for mcs51, the ticket's `test2.c` gets warning 112, error 101, and then the internal
error "node PARAM shouldn't be processed here". The compiler gives these three messages with the
small model, the large model, and `--stack-auto`. The internal error does not need a function
without a declaration. This file gets it after error 101:

```c
extern void g (int);
extern int h (void);

void f (void) { g (h (1, 2)); }
```

An inner call with two or more arguments also gets the internal error after error 102, "too few
parameters", and after error 78, "incompatible types". The internal error does not occur when the
parameter of the outer function has the type `char`.

## Cause

`decorateType()` in `src/SDCCast.c` turns the tree of an expression with an error into a `NULLOP`
node of type `char` and sets `isError`. `processParms()` does not test `isError` after it
decorates an argument. When `char` needs a conversion to the type of the parameter,
`processParms()` casts a copy of the tree and decorates the cast. `copyAst()` does not copy
`isError`, so `decorateType()` decorates both children of the copy. The right child of a call
with two or more arguments is a `PARAM` node, for which `decorateType()` reports the internal
error. In `test2.c` the inner function is not declared. `resolveSymbols()` gives it the type of
`int f (void)`, and the call with two arguments gets error 101.

## Fix

`processParms()` returns 1 when the tree of an argument has `isError` after `decorateType()`. The
outer call becomes an error tree, as it does for the other errors of `processParms()`.

One difference in diagnostics follows. When a call with such an argument is the first statement
of a block, the compiler does not check the other statements of the block, and it gives warning
85 for parameters whose only uses are in the error tree or in those statements. r17228 does that
for other errors in a first statement, for example for `h (x, 2);` with `int h (void)`.

## Verification

`support/valdiag/tests/bug-2639.c` has five cases. In four of them the inner call has too many
arguments. The inner function is not declared in the first, and in the next three the call is the
argument, an operand of the argument, and the first of two arguments. In the fifth case the inner
call has too few arguments. Each inner call is written on two lines, and the internal error has
the number of the second line, where the test does not expect a diagnostic. On r17228 the five
cases fail for mcs51, mcs51-large, and mcs51-stack-auto. With the patch they pass for these
three, z80, and stm8, and the test passes in host mode.

With the patches of this report, the diagnostics suite has 0 failures for mcs51, mcs51-large,
mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8, and the regression suite has 0 failures for host, mcs51-small,
mcs51-medium, mcs51-large, mcs51-huge, mcs51-small-stack-auto, mcs51-large-stack-auto, stm8, and
ucz80. For mcs51-small, the code of every test has the size that it has without the patch.

## Related

- `g (1 + h (1, 2))` gets error 101 and then error 78 with "from type 'void'", with and without
  the patch. `decorateType()` returns the `+` node without a type and without `isError` when its
  right operand has an error.
- `extern int h (); h (1, 2);` stops with the internal error "Setting of register parameter vs.
  other parameter not yet implemented for functions without prototype", with and without the
  patch. The entry for #3481 is about that message.
- A call with arguments of a function without a declaration gets error 101 after warning 112,
  because of the type that `resolveSymbols()` gives the function. C90 6.3.2.2 declares such a
  function as `extern int f ();`. This was compiled with the default standard only.
